title: Shopping
description: Say what you are buying, and what it costs.
grammar: ir + a place, and asking for the price
grammarNote: You say ir a + a place: voy a la tienda. And a price is cuánto cuesta.

explanation.summary: Shopping in Spanish is two pieces of grammar: ir a + a place to say where you are going, and the word for a price. The verb ir is irregular, so it is worth learning its forms now.

sections.heading: Going to the shop
sections.body: Ir is one of the most irregular verbs in Spanish: voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van. After ir you use a instead of de: voy a la tienda, voy al mercado. And the everyday phrase for shopping is ir de compras, not ir a comprar.

examples.en: I am going to the shop.
She is going to the market.

sections.heading: Asking the price
sections.body: The verb for to cost is costar, and it takes the thing first: cuesta diez euros. To ask, put cuánto in front: ¿cuánto cuesta? You can also ask for the price of something specific with cuánto cuesta el abrigo.

sections.heading: Saying what you want
sections.body: Wanting something uses the verb querer, and the thing you want takes un or una: quiero un café, quiero una camisa. If you are asking for something politely, add por favor, which you already know.

items.note: An infinitive ending in -ar: pago, pagas, paga.
An infinitive ending in -ar: compro, compras, compra.
It changes to cara before a feminine noun: una casa cara.
It changes to barata before a feminine noun.
Feminine: la talla. It also means height.
A reflexive verb: me pruebo el abrigo. It keeps the -se ending.
Feminine: la caja. It also means a box.
Feminine: la bolsa. It also means a purse.

drills.meaning: I am going to the shop
drills.note: After ir you use a, not de.
Un agrees with the thing, not the speaker.
Caro becomes cara before a feminine noun.
